verdict.summary: Composio has no managed X app, so you have to register your own. X reviews your stated use case when you open a developer account. The wait is undocumented: reports range from near-instant to about two weeks. Once you have an app, any X user can authorize it. There is no separate verification and no marketplace review. The real limits are pay-per-use billing and X's policy rules on write actions such as likes, follows and replies.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 1-2 hours (account, billing, app config, privacy policy, test)
verdict.time_to_first_connection: 30-60 min if the developer account is approved right away; up to ~2 weeks if it goes to manual review (reported)
verdict.approval_wait: none to ~2 weeks (reported, no official SLA) for the developer account; no per-app review

gates.name: Approved developer account + app with OAuth 2.0 enabled
gates.unlocks: You can authorize your own X account through your app via Composio and make API calls, as long as you have pay-per-use credits.
limits: Use case must be stated and is reviewed by X; changing the use case later needs prior approval
Default cap of 10 apps per account
Access tokens expire after 2 hours unless offline.access is requested
API calls are billed pay-per-use (e.g. $0.015 per post, $0.20 for a post containing a URL)
gates.time_to_reach: 30-60 min of setup, plus a developer-account review that may take minutes to ~2 weeks (reported)

gates.name: Other X users authorize the same app (no test-user allowlist found)
gates.unlocks: Invited users and teammates can connect their X accounts. The findings show no test-user list or install cap for OAuth apps.
limits: Posting caps reported by a third-party guide: 100 posts per 15 min per user, 10,000 per 24 h per app
User-context Tweet/user lookups: 900 requests per 15 min per app
Following, likes and quote-posts are unavailable on all self-serve tiers (April 2026)
Self-serve replies are only allowed when the original author mentioned or quoted the replying account
gates.time_to_reach: Same as Gate 1, no extra step

gates.name: Public production use (policy compliance, no listing review)
gates.unlocks: Any X user can connect. No marketplace or app-directory review was found. Production access depends on staying compliant with the Developer Policy and Automation Rules and on paying for a suitable tier.
limits: Commercial use needs a paid tier (the free tier is non-commercial only)
Up to 3 apps (dev/staging/prod) per service; dev and staging apps may not be used in production
X may audit compliance once a year and may suspend access without notice
gates.time_to_reach: Same as Gate 1, plus time to publish a privacy policy and build the consent UX

steps.title: Verify email and phone on your X account
steps.detail: Use the X account that will own the app. Make sure it has a verified email address and phone number, because X may require both before you can apply for a developer account.

steps.title: Sign up in the Developer Console and describe your use case
steps.detail: Sign in to console.x.com with your X account. Accept the Developer Agreement and Policy, then fill in the profile that describes how you will use the API. Be specific about what your agent reads and writes, because X reviews every proposed use and will not approve apps that have no use case.
gotchas: If you change the use case later, you need X's approval first.
An agent can draft the use-case text for you, but you have to submit it under your own identity.

steps.title: Wait for developer account approval if prompted
steps.detail: The console's getting-started steps don't mention a wait, but X's policy says each use case is reviewed. Forum reports from 2023 describe waits of about two weeks. A 2026 third-party guide says simple use cases are often approved quickly.
gotchas: X publishes no official turnaround time.

steps.title: Set up billing (pay-per-use credits)
steps.detail: New developers use pay-per-use credits, set up under billing in the Developer Console. Saving your first payment card earns a one-time $20 credit, and X matches up to $50 of your first auto-recharge. These credits expire 3 months after they are granted.
gotchas: Commercial use needs a paid tier because the free tier is non-commercial only.
Free scaled access for Public Utility apps is not self-serve and goes through manual review.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: In the Developer Console, click New App and give it a name that identifies your service. If you also want dev and staging apps, you can have up to 3 in total for one service, and each must be labeled clearly.
gotchas: Registering several apps for the same or overlapping use cases is against policy.
Dev and staging apps may not be used in production.

steps.title: Enable OAuth 2.0 in User authentication settings
steps.detail: Open App settings and go to the authentication settings. Turn on OAuth 2.0 and choose Web App as the app type, so the app is a confidential client and gets a Client Secret. Add the callback URL exactly as Composio shows it.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: X checks callback URLs by exact match, so a trailing slash or a different path will cause authorization to fail.
Native App and Single page App are public clients and get no Client Secret.

steps.title: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret immediately
steps.detail: Store the OAuth 2.0 Client ID and Client Secret in a secrets manager as soon as they appear. The console shows credentials only once. If you lose them, regenerating creates new ones and invalidates the old ones.

steps.title: Create the Composio auth config with a trimmed scope list
steps.detail: In Composio, create an auth config for the twitter toolkit using your own Client ID and Client Secret. Keep offline.access so you get refresh tokens. Remove like.write and follows.write, because X has removed liking and following from all self-serve tiers.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Composio's default scopes don't include users.email. Add it if you need the user's email address.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection through Composio and approve it at x.com/i/oauth2/authorize. Then make a read call, for example looking up the authenticated user, to confirm the token works. The code-for-token exchange has to finish within 30 seconds, which Composio does automatically.
gotchas: A wrong Client ID doesn't produce an error on the authorize page. The problem only shows up after you log in, so check the ID carefully.

steps.title: Publish a privacy policy and build the consent UX
steps.detail: Draft and publish a privacy policy that covers what you collect, how you share it (including with X) and how to contact you. Show it before anyone signs up. Add an explicit consent step before the agent posts or takes other actions for a user. Signing in alone does not count as consent.
gotchas: If you offer Sign in with X, it must be at least as prominent as any other sign-in option, and you must show the user's X handle and avatar after they sign in.
Never ask users for their X password.

steps.title: Open to users and stay within the Automation Rules
steps.detail: Share the connection flow with your users. Check that your agent follows the Automation Rules. Automated accounts must have the 'Automated' profile label, there must be no bulk or spam actions, and replies are limited to cases where the original author mentioned or quoted the account. Watch posting volume against per-user and per-app limits.
gotchas: X can suspend apps without explaining why, so keep a record of how you comply with the policy.

requirements.item: Approved developer account with a stated use case
requirements.detail: X reviews every proposed use of the platform and will not approve apps that have no use case.

requirements.item: Verified email and phone on the X account
requirements.detail: May be required before you can apply for a developer account.

requirements.item: OAuth 2.0 enabled with an exact-match callback URL
requirements.detail: Turn on OAuth 2.0 in the app's authentication settings and register the Composio callback URL exactly as shown.

requirements.item: Confidential app type (Web App) for a Client Secret
requirements.detail: Web App and Automated App or bot types get a Client Secret. Native App and Single page App types do not.

requirements.item: Pay-per-use credits or a paid tier
requirements.detail: New developers are on pay-per-use. Commercial use needs a paid tier.
It must cover what you collect, how you share it (including with X) and how to contact you.
Get explicit consent before posting, following or changing a user's profile. Authentication alone is not consent.

scopes.effect: Basic read access. The findings show no extra review for these scopes.
Needed to get a refresh token. Without it, access tokens expire after 2 hours.
No scope review was found, but each post is billed ($0.015, or $0.20 with a URL), and self-serve replies only work when the original author mentioned or quoted the account.
These scopes are in Composio's defaults, but the like and follow endpoints were removed from all self-serve tiers in April 2026. Drop them unless you have Enterprise access.
Needed to read the user's email address. It is not in Composio's defaults, so add it by hand if you need it.
X does not classify these scopes, but the Automation Rules require explicit consent before sending automated DMs.

blockers.symptom: Developer account application stays pending, or the app is not approved
blockers.cause: X reviews the use case manually, and apps with no clear use case are rejected
blockers.fix: Write a specific use case that says what the app reads and writes, and wait. Reported waits are up to about two weeks.

blockers.symptom: Like or follow actions fail even though the user granted the scopes
blockers.cause: Following, likes and quote-posts were removed from all self-serve tiers in April 2026
blockers.fix: Remove like.write and follows.write from the Composio scopes and don't build features that depend on them.

blockers.cause: Self-serve tiers only allow replies when the original author mentioned or quoted the replying account
blockers.fix: Only reply to posts where the account was summoned, or move to Enterprise.

blockers.symptom: Authorization fails after login, with a callback or redirect error
blockers.cause: The callback URL doesn't exactly match the one registered in the app, or the Client ID is wrong
blockers.fix: Paste the Composio callback URL exactly into User authentication settings and check the Client ID again.

blockers.symptom: App shows as Suspended in the Developer Console
blockers.cause: X enforced a policy violation, such as automation spam, selling actions or scraping, and may not say why
blockers.fix: Review the Developer Policy and Automation Rules, then file a review request on the developer forum.

blockers.cause: No pay-per-use credits, or the free credits have expired
blockers.fix: Save a payment card and add credits in the Developer Console's billing section. Promotional credits expire after 3 months.

composio.note: Composio has no managed OAuth app for X, so you must register your own app in the Developer Console and give Composio its Client ID and Client Secret (choose the Web App type so you get a secret). Add Composio's callback URL to the app's User authentication settings exactly as shown. Composio's default scopes include like.write and follows.write. X removed those actions from all self-serve tiers in April 2026, so remove them from the auth config.

evidence.claim: Sign-up is through console.x.com: the developer signs in with an X account, accepts the Developer Agreement and Policy, and completes a profile describing intended API use.
evidence.quote: Visit console.x.com and sign in with your X account.

evidence.claim: Since Feb 23, 2026, programmatic replies via POST /2/tweets are only allowed when the original author has summoned the replier by mention or quote; this applies to self-serve tiers only.
evidence.quote: These changes affect self-serve tiers only — Enterprise access is not impacted.

evidence.claim: Per-user and per-app posting caps: a third-party guide says POST /2/tweets allows 100 posts per 15 minutes per connected account (user token) and 10,000 per 24 hours per app across all accounts.
evidence.quote: There is a per-user limit of 100 posts per 15 minutes

evidence.claim: Developer account FAQ caps accounts at 10 apps by default to combat spam; more than 10 requires an elevation request, and X will not approve apps without a stated use case.
evidence.quote: We will not approve Apps that do not include a use case.

evidence.claim: Developer Policy allows up to 3 apps for dev, staging and production instances of one service, all registered to one account and labeled as such; dev or staging apps may not be used in production.
evidence.quote: you may create and use a maximum of 3 applications for development, staging, and production instances of the same service.

evidence.claim: Policy forbids registering several apps for one use case or overlapping use cases; white-label versions need separate approval.
evidence.quote: You may not register multiple applications for a single use case or substantially similar or overlapping use cases.

evidence.claim: Redirect URI must match one of the callback URLs saved in the app's settings, using exact-match validation.
evidence.quote: For OAuth 2.0, you will need to have exact match validation for your callback URL.

evidence.claim: OAuth 2.0 has to be switched on in the app's authentication settings in the Developer Console before a Client ID is shown.
evidence.quote: To enable OAuth 2.0 in your App, you must enable it in your App's authentication settings found in the App settings section of the Developer Console.

evidence.claim: App type sets confidentiality: Native App and Single page App are public clients with no secret; Web App and Automated App or bot are confidential clients that receive a Client Secret.
evidence.quote: Native App and Single page Apps are public clients and Web App and Automated App or bots are confidential clients.

evidence.claim: Access tokens last two hours by default; a refresh token is only issued when the offline.access scope is requested.
evidence.quote: the access token you create through the Authorization Code Flow with PKCE will only stay valid for two hours unless you've used the offline.access scope.

evidence.claim: An older developer support FAQ says a new app requires an approved developer account, and the application ends with an email confirmation step.
evidence.quote: If you plan to create a new App for new credentials, you must have an approved developer account.

evidence.claim: Authorization codes expire 30 seconds after approval, so the code must be exchanged for a token within that window.
evidence.quote: The auth_code has a time limit of 30 seconds

evidence.claim: Scopes are requested as fine-grained values in the authorize URL; the documented catalog covers reading and writing tweets, users, follows, likes, lists, blocks, bookmarks, mutes, DMs, broadcasts and media, plus offline.access.
evidence.quote: tweet.read | All the Tweets you can view, including Tweets from protected accounts.

evidence.claim: The scope-to-endpoint mapping is a separate X guide; the authorization-code page does not mark any scope as sensitive or restricted, and no review tier for scopes was found in the pages I read.
evidence.quote: To learn more about what scopes map to what endpoints, view our authentication mapping guide.

evidence.claim: Email retrieval needs the users.email scope, which is in the documented catalog but is not in Composio's default scope list.
evidence.quote: users.email | Email from an authenticated user.

evidence.claim: Policy requires express, informed consent from each user before the app takes actions for them, such as posting, following or changing profile information; authentication alone is not consent.
evidence.quote: a person authenticating into your service does not by itself constitute consent.

evidence.claim: The privacy policy must be shown before a user can download, install or sign up, and must cover what is collected, how it is shared (including with X) and a contact route.
evidence.quote: You must display your service's privacy policy to people before they are permitted to download, install, or sign up to your service.

evidence.claim: Sign in with X must be shown at least as prominently as any other sign-in option, and once a user signs in, their X identity (handle, avatar, X logo) must be displayed.
evidence.quote: The Sign in with X option must be displayed at least as prominently as any other sign-up or sign-in feature on your service.

evidence.claim: Apps may not store X passwords or ask users for their X password or consumer key; Sign-in with X is the recommended method.
evidence.quote: You may not store X passwords, or request that people provide their X password

evidence.claim: Policy bars selling or receiving compensation for X actions such as posts, follows, reposts, likes and replies.
evidence.quote: As you use the X API you may not sell or receive monetary or virtual compensation for any X actions.

evidence.claim: Apps that perform write actions must follow the Automation Rules, including explicit consent before automated replies or DMs and no bulk or spammy actions; automated accounts must be labeled and linked to a human-managed account.
evidence.quote: Enable the 'Automated' profile label

evidence.claim: The Developer Policy says every new developer must apply for a developer account, and X reviews each proposed use case before granting and maintaining access; changes to the use case need prior approval.
evidence.quote: We review all proposed uses of the X developer platform to verify policy compliance

evidence.claim: Likes must be directly initiated by the authenticated user; auto-liking, bulk liking and selling likes are prohibited for all apps.
evidence.quote: Likes must be directly initiated by the authenticated user.

evidence.claim: Scraping or browser automation instead of the official API is prohibited and can result in permanent suspension; benchmarking X against competitors is also prohibited.
evidence.quote: Non-API access — Prohibited—scraping and browser automation = permanent ban

evidence.claim: Commercial use requires an appropriate paid tier, because the free tier is non-commercial only; government use requires an Enterprise tier.
evidence.quote: free tier is non-commercial only

evidence.claim: X may suspend or permanently revoke API access for policy violations and may audit compliance up to once a year.
evidence.quote: we may suspend or permanently revoke your access to the X API and X Content.

evidence.claim: A developer forum post reports an app shown as Suspended in the Developer Console with no reason given by email or notification, which shows enforcement can happen without notice.
evidence.quote: I have not received any email or notification explaining the reason for the suspension.

evidence.claim: Developer account approval timing: 2023 forum threads report waits of about two weeks, and some applicants were still pending after three weeks; no official SLA was found.
evidence.quote: This process typically takes about two weeks or so.

evidence.claim: A third-party 2026 guide says straightforward applications are often approved quickly, while complex use cases may get manual review lasting hours to days; not an official X statement.
evidence.quote: Complex use cases involving bulk data or large-scale automation may trigger manual review lasting hours to days.

evidence.claim: No marketplace or app directory for third-party X apps appeared in X's docs or my searches, so no listing review was identified for a self-built OAuth app.
Rate limits for OAuth 2.0 user-context Tweet and user lookups are 900 requests per 15 minutes per app, up from 300 under OAuth 1.0a.
evidence.quote: We are increasing the per-App limit from 300 to 900 requests per 15 minutes

evidence.claim: Changelog history: like and follow endpoints were removed from the Free tier on Aug 22, 2025, and removed from all self-serve tiers in April 2026; Composio's default scopes still list like and follow scopes.
evidence.quote: we removed POST /2/users/:id/likes and POST /2/users/:id/following from the X API Free tier

evidence.claim: The Developer Console is where apps are created, credentials generated, and billing managed; the console's own getting-started steps (sign up, accept agreement, New App) do not mention a waiting period.
evidence.quote: Create apps, generate credentials, monitor usage, and manage billing—all in one place.

evidence.claim: Developer Console is at console.x.com and the older developer.x.com portal URL redirects to an X login wall when probed, so the console must be reached with an X account.
evidence.quote: login_wall: true

evidence.claim: Probe: the X authorize endpoint responds with 200 and an 'Authorize app' login page when given an invalid client_id, and returns no OAuth error parameters in the response, so the client_id check is not visible until login.
Probe: x.com does not serve OpenID Connect discovery (404 at /.well-known/openid-configuration), so X's OAuth endpoints must be taken from its docs.
Credentials are shown only once in the console; if lost they must be regenerated, which invalidates the old ones.
evidence.quote: API keys and tokens are only displayed once when generated.

evidence.claim: Getting Access lists Client ID and Secret as the credentials for OAuth 2.0 user-context requests, alongside API Key/Secret and Bearer Token.
evidence.quote: OAuth 2.0 authentication for user-context requests.

evidence.claim: The application may require email and phone verification on the X account before a developer account can be applied for.
evidence.quote: the email and phone number verification from your X account may be needed to apply for a developer account

evidence.claim: Access model per the Feb 6, 2026 changelog: pay-per-use credits for new developers; Basic and Pro remain for existing subscribers; Public Utility Apps keep free scaled access.
evidence.quote: Public Utility Apps continue to receive free scaled access.

evidence.claim: New pay-per-use accounts can earn one-time free credits: $20 for saving a first payment card, and a match of up to $50 for the first auto-recharge. Credits expire 3 months after they are granted.
evidence.quote: a one-time $20 when an account saves its first eligible payment card

evidence.claim: Following, likes and quote-posts via the API were removed from all self-serve tiers, effective with the April 20, 2026 pricing update; POST /2/tweets is $0.015 per post and $0.20 when the post contains a URL.
evidence.quote: Following, Likes, and Quote-Posts via the API have been removed from all self-serve tiers.

open_questions: X publishes no official turnaround time for developer account approval; the only timing figures come from 2023 forum posts and a third-party 2026 guide.
X doesn't say whether every application is reviewed by hand or whether simple use cases are approved automatically.
No official list of sensitive or restricted scopes needing extra review was found.
It is unconfirmed whether X still grants mute, block and DM write scopes to self-serve apps after the April 2026 changes.
Not checked against a live Composio config: the exact callback URL to register. Copy it from your Composio auth config.
No official per-app install cap for OAuth users was found. The posting limits come from a third-party guide, and X's official rate-limit table was not read.
